Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-6391", "title": "Mitochondrial Diseases", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Metabolism is the process your body uses to make energy from the food you eat."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Food is made up of proteins, carbohydrates, and fats."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Chemicals in your digestive system (enzymes) break the food parts down into sugars and acids, your body's fuel."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Your body can use this fuel right away, or it can store the energy in your body tissues."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "If you have a metabolic disorder , something goes wrong with this process."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Mitochondrial diseases are a group of metabolic disorders."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Mitochondria are small structures that produce energy in almost all of your cells."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "They make it by combining oxygen with the fuel molecules (sugars and fats) that come from your food."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "When the mitochondria are defective, the cells do not have enough energy."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "The unused oxygen and fuel molecules build up in the cells and cause damage."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The symptoms of mitochondrial disease can vary."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "It depends on how many mitochondria are defective, and where they are in the body."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Sometimes only one organ, tissue, or cell type is affected."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "But often the problem affects many of them."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Muscle and nerve cells have especially high energy needs, so muscular and neurological problems are common."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "They usually happen before age 20, and some are more common in infants."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "There are no cures for these diseases, but treatments may help with symptoms and slow down the disease."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "They may include physical therapy, vitamins and supplements, special diets, and medicines."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1540", "title": "Cancer--Living with Cancer", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Learning to live with cancer Cancer is a common disease."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Many Americans will be diagnosed with cancer during their lifetimes."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Even though cancer may be life-threatening, many people have successful treatment."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Others live with cancer for a very long time."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "For most people with cancer, learning to live with the disease is one of the biggest challenges they've ever faced."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "That's because having cancer touches just about every part of your life and the lives of those around you."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Cancer and its treatment may change: Your daily routines and ability to work Your important relationships The way you look, feel, and think about yourself If you learn what to expect, you may feel more in control and prepared to cope with these changes."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Your health care provider can help you find information and support services that are right for you."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Coping with feelings about having cancer Having cancer may cause a range of strong emotions, such as sadness, anger, fear, worry, or guilt."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "These feelings are normal, and they're likely to change over time."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "It's helpful to sort out your feelings in a way that's comfortable for you."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "You might try: Talking openly with someone you trust Writing about your feelings Using relaxation methods, such as meditation and other complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) Doing the things you enjoy, giving yourself a break from focusing on cancer If your emotions seem to take over your life, tell your provider."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "You may need extra support if you have symptoms of depression , stress , anxiety , or panic disorder ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Communicating with your health care team During cancer treatment, you usually have a team of providers."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Along with doctors and nurses, you may be able to talk with social workers, pharmacists, dietitians, and other health professionals."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "These professionals are prepared to help you deal with the issues that cancer brings up, including concerns about finances ."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "But it's up to you to let your team know what's on your mind."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Good communication with your providers may help you feel more in control and satisfied with your care."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Your communications may be better if you: Tell your providers how much you want to know about your cancer and its treatment."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Do you want all the details or just the big picture?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Write down your questions and concerns before your visits."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Bring a family member or a friend to your visits."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "This person can help by listening, taking notes, and asking questions."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Talking openly with family and friends Cancer changes the daily routines and roles of the people who love and support you."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "They may need to start doing the things you've always done for them."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "And you may need their help doing things you've always done for yourself."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "These changes can be difficult for everyone."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "It may help to have an honest talk about changing roles and needs."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "If that sounds too hard, ask a social worker or another member of your care team to help you talk with family and friends who are helping with your care."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "These caregivers may need some support , too."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Dealing with changes in your self-image Cancer and its treatment may cause some big changes in how you look, feel, and think about yourself."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "For example, you may have: Less energy Temporary or permanent changes in your body, such as scars , or hair loss from chemotherapy Problems being sexually close or doubts about dating Coping with these changes can be hard."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "But most people find ways to feel more positive over time."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "If you feel well enough, you might try: Exercise ."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Walking, yoga, or other types of movement may help you feel stronger and more in control of your body."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Staying involved in life and helping others."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Think about volunteering, hobbies, or other activities that might make you feel good about yourself."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Talking with a professional, either with a partner or on your own, may help."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Adjusting to life after treatment After treatment, you'll have regular cancer follow-up care."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Your provider will explain the schedule of checkups and tests you'll need."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "This is a good time to discuss the challenges you may face ahead."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Knowing what to expect may help you make plans as you find a \"new normal\" with cancer as part of your life."}]}, {"id": "MLP-481", "title": "Kaposi Sarcoma", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Kaposi sarcoma, sometimes called KS, is a type of cancer."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It causes lesions (abnormal tissue) to grow in different parts of the body, including: The skin Lymph nodes Mucous membranes (the lining of the mouth, nose, and throat) Other organs These lesions are usually red or purple."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They are made of cancer cells, new blood vessels, and blood cells."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The lesions may begin in more than one place in the body at the same time."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "This makes Kaposi sarcoma different from other cancers."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "What causes Kaposi sarcoma and who is more likely to develop it?"}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Kaposi sarcoma is caused by infection with human herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8)."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "This virus is also called Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV)."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Most people infected with this virus don't get Kaposi sarcoma."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "But certain people who get this virus are more likely to develop one of the types of Kaposi sarcoma: People with weakened immune systems due to HIV can develop epidemic (HIV-associated) Kaposi sarcoma."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "People with weakened immune systems due to medicines they need to take after an organ transplant can develop iatrogenic (transplant-related) Kaposi sarcoma."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Older men of Mediterranean or Eastern European Jewish heritage can develop classic Kaposi sarcoma."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Young men in Africa can develop endemic (African) Kaposi sarcoma."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "What are the symptoms of Kaposi sarcoma?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Kaposi sarcoma usually starts out as one or more red, purple, or brown skin lesions on the legs and feet."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "They are most often on the ankles or soles of the feet."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Over time, lesions may form in other parts of the body."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "But sometimes the lesions can cause problems, especially as you get more of them and they grow bigger."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "For example: Pressure from the lesions may block the flow of lymph and blood in the legs and cause painful swelling If lesions grow in your stomach or intestines, they can bleed and may cause abdominal (belly) pain and diarrhea Lesions in the lungs can also bleed and may cause shortness of breath How is Kaposi sarcoma diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "To find out whether you have Kaposi sarcoma, your health care provider: Will ask about your medical and family history Will do a physical exam May order a chest x-ray to look for Kaposi sarcoma in the lungs May do a biopsy to check for Kaposi sarcoma lesions in the skin May do an endoscopy to check for Kaposi sarcoma in the stomach and intestines May do a bronchoscopy to check for Kaposi sarcoma in the lungs If you do have Kaposi sarcoma, you will likely need blood and imaging tests to find out if the cancer has spread to other parts of the body."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "What are the treatments for Kaposi sarcoma?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Which treatment(s) you get will depend on The type of Kaposi sarcoma you have How many lesions you have and where in the body they are What kinds of problems the lesions are causing Your overall health For people who have epidemic (HIV-associated) Kaposi sarcoma, taking HIV medicines may be enough to treat the Kaposi sarcoma."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "For people who have iatrogenic (transplant-related) Kaposi sarcoma, changing the dose of the medicines or switching medicines may be helpful."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "But some people with these types of Kaposi sarcoma will need additional treatment."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "The treatment options for Kaposi sarcoma may include: Radiation therapy Surgery Cryosurgery, a treatment that uses an instrument to freeze and destroy abnormal tissue Chemotherapy Immunotherapy NIH: National Cancer Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-6909", "title": "VLDL Cholesterol", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance that's found in all the cells in your body."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Your liver makes cholesterol, and it is also in some foods, such as meat and dairy products."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Your body needs some cholesterol to work properly."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "But having too much cholesterol in your blood raises your risk of coronary artery disease ."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "VLDL stands for very-low-density lipoprotein."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Your liver makes VLDL and releases it into your bloodstream."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The VLDL particles mainly carry triglycerides , another type of fat, to your tissues."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "VLDL is similar to LDL cholesterol , but LDL mainly carries cholesterol to your tissues instead of triglycerides."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "VLDL and LDL are sometimes called \"bad\" cholesterols because they can contribute to the buildup of plaque in your arteries."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "This buildup is called atherosclerosis ."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The plaque that builds up is a sticky substance made up of fat, cholesterol, calcium, and other substances found in the blood."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Over time, the plaque hardens and narrows your arteries."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "This limits the flow of oxygen-rich blood to your body."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "It can lead to coronary artery disease and other heart diseases ."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "There isn't a way to directly measure your VLDL level."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Instead, you will most likely get a blood test to measure your triglyceride level."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "The lab can use your triglyceride level to estimate what your VLDL level is."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Your VLDL is about one-fifth of your triglyceride level."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "However, estimating your VLDL this way does not work if your triglyceride level is very high."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Your VLDL level should be less than 30 mg/dL (milligrams per deciliter)."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Anything higher than that puts you at risk of heart disease and stroke ."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Because VLDL and triglycerides are linked, you can lower your VLDL level by lowering your triglyceride level."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "You may be able to lower your triglycerides with a combination of losing weight, changing your diet, and getting exercise."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "It is important to switch to healthy fats and cut back on sugar and alcohol."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Some people may also need to take medicines."}]}, {"id": "MLP-5419", "title": "After Surgery", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "After any operation , you'll have some side effects."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "There is usually some pain with surgery."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "There may also be swelling and soreness around the area that the surgeon cut."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Your surgeon can tell you which side effects to expect."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "These are unplanned events linked to the operation."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Some complications are infection, too much bleeding, reaction to anesthesia , or accidental injury."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Some people have a greater risk of complications because of other medical conditions."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Your surgeon can tell you how you might feel and what you will be able to do - or not do - the first few days, weeks, or months after surgery."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Some other questions to ask are: How long you will be in the hospital What kind of supplies, equipment, and help you might need when you go home When you can go back to work When it is ok to start exercising again Are there any other restrictions in your activities Following your surgeon's advice can help you recover as soon as possible."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality"}]}]
